text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- All newspapers front Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim that Malaysia will not allow too much speculation in the ringgit, but will broadly let market forces determine the currency's level. He said the ringgit would recover soon after the speculation phase is over.

-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric project is heading for a delay due to a row between Ekran Bhd, which was awarded the privatisation, and ABB Asea Brown Boveri, one of two main contractors building the dam and power generation facilities.

-- The company organising the 1998 Commonwealth Games in Kuala Lumpur has drawn up a 14.6 million ringgit plan to publicise the games. It has received severe criticism from the government for lagging on the promotional front.

-- Poor productivity in Malaysia attracted speculation in the ringgit. The low producitivity led to greater current account deficit and sluggish export growth, according to Capital Dynamics, the publisher of weekly "i Capital".
-- The soon-to-be-listed Utama Banking Group is seeking Tier-1 status for its Bank Utama (M) Bhd.
-- Malaysia Mining Corporation said it has signed an agreement to take up stake in North Petroleum Plc of Britain. The stake will soon be increased to 48 percent.
-- Malaysia's Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was no fear of the economy overheating. He said the projections by analysts were "irresponsible".

-- Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar told Parliament that the sluggishness on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange was due to more attractive alternatives for foreign investors in Latin America and Eastern Europe.
